title: Understanding Social Institutions : Marriage and Family

questions.question: Definethe term social institution. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Social Institution: A structured system of norms and values governing specific
  • aspects of social life, such as family, education, or religion. [U]/[CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Identify one social reform movement in 19th-century India that influenced marriage practices. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Social Reform Movement: The Brahmo Samaj, led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy,
  • reformed marriage practices by opposing child marriage and promoting widow
  • remarriage. [U]/[CO1]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain postmodern views on the changing meaning of marriage in the 21st century. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Postmodern Views: Marriage is seen as fluid, negotiated, and individualized
  • rather than permanent or institutionally fixed. [U]/[CO2]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: State the focus of Symbolic Interactionism in family studies. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Symbolic Interactionism: Focuses on micro-level meanings people assign to
  • family roles and interactions. [U]/[CO2]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define disruptive family dynamics in your own words. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Disruptive Family Dynamics: Patterns of conflict, abuse, or neglect that disturb

questions.question: Define what a protection order is. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Protection Order: A legal measure preventing an abuser from contacting or
  • approaching the victim. [U]/[CO4]

questions.question: Summarize the central concern of Conflict Theory in marriage. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Identify and describe two legal conditions under which a marriage can be declared void in India. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Void Marriage: Declared invalid if prohibited degrees of relationship exist or
  • either party is already married. [U]/[CO4]

questions.question: How does the rise in the single population affect housing or urban lifestyles? / [CO5] [2x13 = 26]
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of Single Population: Increases demand for individual housing and alters
  • urban lifestyle patterns. [A]/[CO5]
  • Part – B
  • 17a. Emergence of Sociology from Revolutions [U]/[CO1]
  • The Enlightenment fostered rational inquiry; the French Revolution
  • challenged feudalism and hierarchy; the Industrial Revolution generated
  • new urban classes and social problems. Together they institutionalised
  • sociology as a science addressing order and change.
  • 17b. Berger’s “Professional Peeper” Metaphor [U]/[CO1]
  • Berger’s metaphor captures the sociologist’s curiosity and moral
  • responsibility. The sociologist observes everyday life critically yet ethically,
  • unveiling taken-for-granted norms without voyeurism. It balances
  • detachment with empathy.
  • 18a. Education, Digitalisation, and Youth Identity
  • [An]/[CO3]
  • Digital technology shapes self-presentation, community, and values. In
  • Kerala, access to education and online culture reconfigures class, language,
  • and gender relations, creating hybrid youth identities and new social
  • networks.
  • 18b. Transformation of Matrilineal System in Kerala
  • [An]/[CO3]
  • Transition from taravad (matrilineal joint family) to nuclear units eroded
  • female property rights but promoted individual autonomy. Legal reforms
  • (Marumakkathayam Act 1933) shifted inheritance and authority, redefining
  • gender dynamics.
  • 19a. Social Change and Indian National Movement
  • [An]/[CO3]
  • The movement fostered unity across caste and religion, promoted women’s
  • participation, and laid foundations of democratic citizenship. It embedded
  • nationalism within everyday moral life.
  • 19b. Tradition and Modernity in India [An]/[CO3]
  • Indian modernity fuses continuity with change—ritual coexistence with
  • technology, caste persistence with new mobility. Sociological duality reveals
  • adaptation rather than rupture.
  • 20a. Functions of Mass Media [U]/[CO4]
  • Media informs, educates, entertains, and socialises citizens, linking
  • individuals to the public sphere. It reinforces norms but also stimulates
  • reform through exposure and debate.
  • 20b. Glocalization in Culture [A]/[CO4]
  • Global brands adapt to local tastes—McDonald’s India offers vegetarian
  • menus; fashion integrates traditional motifs with modern design. This
  • hybridization preserves cultural identity while embracing global influence.
